questions.enonce: According to the introductory lecture, what are the four main sub-processes into which production management is divided?
options: Managing raw materials, managing production resources, managing flows, and managing people.
Sales forecasting, product design, financial auditing, and human resources recruitment.
Purchasing raw materials, equipment maintenance, quality testing, and customer delivery.
Inventory control, facility layout, marketing strategy, and cost accounting.
questions.explication: The lecture clearly outlines four main sub-processes: managing raw materials, managing production resources, managing flows, and managing people[span_0](start_span)[span_0](end_span).

questions.enonce: Why is the forecasting of global demand considered one of the most important processes in production management?
options: Because without it, a company cannot assemble and manufacture the products necessary for its market and customers[span_1](start_span)[span_1](end_span).
Because it eliminates the need for any inventory storage.
Because it dictates the exact salary of every factory worker.
Because it replaces the need for procurement processes.
questions.explication: Demand forecasting is critical because failing to forecast demand means the company cannot properly assemble and manufacture products for its market and customers[span_2](start_span)[span_2](end_span).

questions.enonce: What does the task of scheduling production work involve on a day-to-day basis?
options: Defining the activities to be performed on production lines and workshops, specifying what is manufactured on each equipment at specific times[span_3](start_span)[span_3](end_span).
Negotiating long-term contracts with external raw material suppliers.
Calculating the annual profit margins for retail prices.
Recruiting specialized workers and planning training schedules.
questions.explication: Scheduling work means day-to-day definition of activities on production lines, specifying which products are made on specific equipment at designated times[span_4](start_span)[span_4](end_span).

questions.enonce: What negative consequence can arise from unbalanced workloads between equipment or employees?
options: Low rentability of equipment investments, underuse, and stress/frustration among employees working at different capacities[span_5](start_span)[span_5](end_span).
An immediate increase in overall product quality and customer satisfaction.
The total elimination of information flows within the company.
A reduction in the time needed for raw material procurement.
questions.explication: Unbalanced workloads lead to poor equipment rentability when idle, and can create stress between employees who feel overworked versus underutilized[span_6](start_span)[span_6](end_span).

questions.enonce: Besides managing physical flows of parts and products, what crucial type of flow must be managed in production?
options: Information flows, such as tracking customer orders, manufacturing orders, and workforce data[span_7](start_span)[span_7](end_span).
Financial cash flows managed exclusively by the marketing department.
External political flows regarding international trade laws.
Direct consumer feedback gathered via social media.
questions.explication: Information flows are vital and include tracking customer orders, manufacturing orders, and workforce data like training and health[span_8](start_span)[span_8](end_span).

questions.enonce: What is one of the key benefits of maintaining a continuous dialogue and collaboration with production teams regarding people management?
options: It enables the continuous improvement of production processes because frontline workers know what is missing or not working properly[span_9](start_span)[span_9](end_span).
It completely removes the need for equipment maintenance.
It allows workers to set their own retail prices.
It guarantees that no employee will ever take a leave of absence.
questions.explication: Collaborating with production teams helps continuously improve processes because workers on the line know firsthand what is missing or failing[span_10](start_span)[span_10](end_span).
